title: Source-artifact contamination and extraction eligibility gate v0
problem: Blocked by ticket-413. Fetchable content is currently treated as analyzable source text even when it is an access challenge, redirect shell, error page, navigation wrapper, or insufficient-content document. These artifacts have produced accepted claims and graph evidence.
acceptance_criteria: A deterministic pre-extraction gate classifies source artifacts as eligible, quarantined, or needs_review and persists stable reason codes and gate version.
Known challenge, redirect, navigation, error-page, empty, and insufficient-content benchmark slices produce zero extraction-eligible chunks and zero accepted claims.
Eligibility uses content and metadata signals rather than domain-specific keywords; legitimate short abstracts remain distinguishable from contaminated shells.
Quarantined sources and gate diagnostics remain private and never enter public exports.
Existing fixture-mode and valid manual-source ingestion behavior remains deterministic.
Benchmark output reports contaminated-source false admissions separately from claim-level false acceptances.
On completion, ticket-415 changes from blocked to ready; no later Phase 4 ticket is activated.
test_plan: With mock-only env: python -m pytest tests/unit/test_source_quality_gate.py tests/unit/test_document_parser.py tests/unit/test_research_quality_benchmark.py -q
With mock-only env: python -m pytest tests/golden -q
With mock-only env: python -m rge.cli verify --skip-site
non_goals: Do not implement semantic claim entailment.
Do not delete quarantined source files or historical database rows.
Do not make live network calls part of tests.
Do not add public ingestion or review routes.
rollback_plan: Revert the source-quality gate integration and tests. Preserve source records and treat the added eligibility fields as ignored if a migration was introduced.
